# Front-end Engineering in Svelte: Comprehensive Learning Guide ## Course Overview This course path introduces **Svelte**, a modern, compiler-driven front-end framework that emphasizes simplicity, reactivity, and performance. Unlike React or Vue, Svelte shifts much of the work to compile time, resulting in minimal runtime overhead and highly readable component code. **Who this is for:** - Front-end developers transitioning to Svelte - Full-stack engineers seeking a lightweight framework - Candidates preparing for Svelte-focused roles or companies - Developers interested in reactive programming patterns **Why it matters for interview prep:** - Svelte is gaining adoption in performance-critical applications - Its unique approach to reactivity and compilation demonstrates deep understanding of JavaScript compilation - Demonstrates familiarity with modern framework concepts (stores, animations, transitions) - Shows ability to learn emerging technologies quickly - Practical Svelte skills are increasingly valued in startups and forward-thinking companies ## Core Topics Covered - **Svelte Fundamentals**: Component syntax, reactive declarations, and two-way binding - **Component Architecture**: Props, slots, lifecycle hooks, and component composition - **Reactivity & State Management**: Reactive variables, stores (writable, readable, derived), and context API - **Styling in Svelte**: Scoped styling, CSS variables, and animation/transition directives - **Forms & Input Handling**: Form binding, validation, and event handling - **Advanced Patterns**: Higher-order components, custom stores, and transitions/animations - **SvelteKit Essentials**: Routing, layouts, data loading, and server-side considerations - **Performance Optimization**: Code splitting, lazy loading, and bundle analysis ## Learning Path Workflow ### **Phase 1: Svelte Basics (Tasks 1–25)** 1. **Set up environment** — Install Node.js, create Svelte project with Vite 2. **Learn component syntax** — `.svelte` file structure, templates, scripts, styles 3. **Master reactivity** — `let` declarations, reactive statements (`$:`), `$` prefix 4. **Understand two-way binding** — `bind:property` directive for form inputs 5. **Practice variables & expressions** — Basic state management within components **Checkpoint**: Build a simple counter, todo input, and dynamic greeting component. ### **Phase 2: Component Composition (Tasks 26–50)** 6. **Props & communication** — Pass data to child components, validate with `export let` 7. **Slots** — Default slots, named slots, and slot forwarding 8. **Event handling** — DOM events, custom events, event modifiers 9. **Lifecycle hooks** — `onMount`, `onDestroy`, `beforeUpdate`, `afterUpdate` 10. **Conditional rendering** — `{#if}`, `{:else}`, `{#each}` blocks **Checkpoint**: Build a multi-component app with nested children, custom events, and dynamic lists. ### **Phase 3: Stores & State (Tasks 51–75)** 11. **Writable stores** — Create shared state with `writable()`, subscribe and update 12. **Readable stores** — Read-only data streams with `readable()` 13. **Derived stores** — Compute values from other stores with `derived()` 14. **Auto-subscription** — Use `$` prefix to automatically subscribe in templates 15. **Custom stores** — Encapsulate logic with factory functions **Checkpoint**: Build a user authentication state system, shopping cart, and real-time data display. ### **Phase 4: Styling & Animation (Tasks 76–85)** 16. **Scoped CSS** — Component-level styles without naming conventions 17. **CSS classes** — Dynamic class binding with `:class` directive 18. **Animations** — `animate:` directive for FLIP-based animations 19. **Transitions** — `transition:` directive with built-in effects (fade, fly, slide) 20. **Custom animations** — Create custom transition and animation functions **Checkpoint**: Build interactive UI with smooth animations, styled forms, and responsive layouts. ### **Phase 5: Forms & Validation (Tasks 86–95)** 21. **Input binding** — Two-way binding for text, number, checkbox, radio, select 22. **Form handling** — Submit handlers, reset, and multi-field forms 23. **Validation patterns** — Real-time validation, error display, and disabled states 24. **Advanced bindings** — Binding to object properties and arrays **Checkpoint**: Build a full registration form with validation and dynamic fields. ### **Phase 6: SvelteKit & Advanced Topics (Tasks 96–105)** 25. **SvelteKit routing** — File-based routing, dynamic routes, and layout nesting 26. **Server-side considerations** — Load functions, server-only code, form actions 27. **Optimization & deployment** — Code analysis, lazy loading, production builds **Checkpoint**: Deploy a multi-page application with data loading and form handling. ## Key Skills You'll Build ### **Reactivity Mastery** - Understand Svelte's compiler-driven reactivity (no virtual DOM needed) - Write clean, declarative reactive code without mutation confusion - Distinguish between reactive declarations and side effects ### **Component Design** - Build reusable, composable components with clear interfaces - Use slots and named slots for flexible composition - Manage component lifecycles and cleanup properly ### **State Management** - Implement centralized state with stores - Choose between writable, readable, and derived stores - Create custom store patterns for complex logic ### **Animations & UX** - Smoothly animate component transitions and property changes - Create delightful interactions with springs and easing functions - Balance performance and visual polish ### **Full-Stack Thinking** - Understand client-side rendering vs. server-side data loading - Implement form actions and progressive enhancement - Recognize when to shift logic to the server ### **Performance Awareness** - Write code that compiles to minimal JavaScript - Understand bundle impact and code splitting - Recognize anti-patterns that bloat the final output ## Sample Problem Types ### **Problem Type 1: Reactive Counter with Limits** **Description**: Build a counter component that increments/decrements within bounds, displays state reactively, and exports the value to a parent component. ```svelte
{value}
``` **Key concepts**: Props validation, reactive variables, event handling, conditional state. --- ### **Problem Type 2: Todo List with Filtering & Persistence** **Description**: Create a todo app with add/remove/toggle functionality, filter by status (all/active/completed), and persist state to localStorage. ```svelte
